endorsements.quote: Validation studies must therefore include diverse populations to ensure equitable performance across all learner and patient demographics.

Trainees must be explicitly taught to critically appraise AI-generated recommendations rather than passively accept them—a competency that the Shin et al. (2024) study suggests may be eroded by uncritical AI use.

unlisted_practices: Institutions must establish clear protocols for data anonymization, secure storage, and restricted access for AI training data.
Obtain explicit patient consent before using clinical materials such as procedural footage in AI training systems.
Establish robust data protection agreements and comply with local and international regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) when training data are transmitted to external cloud servers.
Collect training datasets from multiple clinics and standardize imaging protocols across clinics to ensure data consistency.
Involve clinical ethicists and patient advocates in developing ethically sound AI responses for reproductive medicine training simulations.
Implement a fail-safe escalation mechanism so persistent deficiencies or outlier errors detected by AI in training are flagged for immediate human review.
Retain human experts for summative competency judgments and clinical reasoning guidance in AI-assisted training.
Academic bodies should initiate exploratory discussions on validation pathways, information transparency, and human review for AI-enhanced training tools in reproductive medicine.
Continuously evaluate AI integration in ART training to ensure transparency and support evidence-based learning objectives.

Validate AI-enhanced training platforms through phased empirical research, including pilot, competency outcome, transfer-to-practice, and cost-effectiveness studies, before claiming educational effectiveness.

screen.reason: The paper presents a conceptual proposal/framework for an AI-enhanced training system in assisted reproductive technology and explicitly states it has not yet been implemented or empirically validated.
